==English==
{{wp}}
[[Image:Pelagisches Schleppnetz.jpg|The part marked ''6'' is the '''headline'''|thumb]]

===Alternative forms===
*{{alter|en|head-line|head line}}

===Etymology===
From {{compound|en|head|line}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈhɛd.laɪn/|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-headline.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛdlaɪn|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# ''A rope.''
## {{lb|en|nautical|obsolete}} Any of various type of [[rope]] used to attach a [[sail]] to a [[yard]]. {{defdate|13th–19th c.}}
## {{lb|en|nautical}} A [[rope]] or [[chain]] used to attach the bow of a vessel to the shore or to another vessel. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
## A rope tied to the [[head]] of an [[animal]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
# ''A line, and related senses.''
## {{lb|en|palmistry|usually as two words}} A line stretching diagonally across the [[palm]], said to represent [[mental]] or [[intellectual]] matters. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
## {{lb|en|chiefly|North America|now|rare|as two words}} The [[boundary]] line of a piece of land, used as a reference in [[surveying]] etc. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
## {{lb|en|typography|now|chiefly|historical}} A line drawn across the head of a page, for the title, page number, etc.; also more generally, the space at the top of a page in which this information is positioned. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Joyce Ulysses|26|He held out his copybook. The word ''Sums'' was written on the '''headline'''.}}
## {{lb|en|chiefly|journalism}} A [[heading]] or title at the top of a page or section of text; especially, a brief line in large letters summarising or drawing attention to the following article or similar in a [[magazine]] or [[newspaper]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
##: {{synonyms|en|hed|lead}}
##: {{ux|en|The '''headline''' on today's newspaper reads "John Doe Wins Wood-Splitting Competition."}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|title=Snakes and ladders|url=http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders|date=22 June 2013|volume=407|issue=8841|page=76|passage=From tabloid '''headlines''' insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603180642/http://www.economist.com:80/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders|archivedate=3 June 2017}}
## {{lb|en|entertainment}} The [[top]]-[[bill]]ed [[attraction]]; a [[headliner]].
